relation_semantics.equivalent: Same quantified mathematical target under explicit notation/index adapters; proof verbosity alone does not make a new core.
relation_semantics.strict_specialization: An explicitly scoped theorem subtarget restricts dimensions/hypotheses/error tier of another; whole multipart tasks may still be incomparable. The scope is stated, so this label is not automatic whole-record dedup.
relation_semantics.merely_related: Shared mechanism/example/prerequisite but materially different mathematical obligation; does not imply leakage-free.
relation_semantics.distinct: The enumerated candidate has a different target even after checking the apparent shared notion; not a global claim against every unlisted native.
relation_semantics.unresolved: A faithful semantic conclusion is not justified; contract defect or missing exhaustive evidence remains visible.

records.question: Let H = C^d with the standard inner product of Eq. (2.4), and let |psi> in H be a unit vector, <psi|psi> = 1. Define rho := |psi><psi|. State explicitly which step uses normalization of |psi> and why dropping it breaks the trace condition.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional H = C^d with the standard inner product of Eq. (2.4).
|psi> is a fixed unit vector; density-operator conditions are exactly Definition 2.1.
conventions: Inner product conjugate-linear in the first argument per Eq. (2.4): <psi|phi> = sum_i psi_i^* phi_i.
Pure state = extreme point of the convex set of density operators.

That claim is false for d>=3. Its answer silently reinterprets boundary as extreme points. No clean equivalence/specialization decision may silently repair that question.
Isometric remixing of pure ensembles concerns nonuniqueness of mixed-state decompositions, not density validation and extremality of a fixed rank-one projector.
Rank-one marginal forces a product extension by a purification/Schmidt argument; the support-one-dimensional principle is shared but the target is a distinct extension/monogamy theorem.

records.dimension_hypothesis_norm_comparison: Legacy d arbitrary with a fixed unit vector and conjugate-linear first inner-product argument. For d>=2, in the trace-one Hermitian affine space the relative boundary of the density set consists of rank-deficient states: positive-definite states have a positive minimum eigenvalue and a neighborhood in that affine space remains positive; a zero-eigenvalue state can be perturbed negatively in that eigendirection and compensating positively in another to preserve trace. In d3, diag(1/2,1/2,0) is therefore a mixed rank2 boundary point and is nonextreme. In the ambient full Hermitian space every trace-one state is boundary because the trace hyperplane has empty interior. For d1 the state set is a singleton equal to its trace-one affine ambient space, so its relative boundary is empty even though its only state is pure.
